# Evaluating XGBoost with SHAP for Questionnaire-Based Risk Screening of Anemia and Chronic Energy Deficiency in Pregnant Women: A Case Study in North Lombok

*Full report generated by experiments/15_paper_report.py on 2026-10-28 13:19 from git commit c033eb2 (run hash ccb36f47646ab009). Every number is read from the result tables named in each section. Prose is a draft for the author to edit. Internal validation on one regional dataset only.*

## Abstract (draft)

Field data from pregnant women in North Lombok were used to estimate hemoglobin (Hb) and the risk of chronic energy deficiency (CED) from questionnaire answers only. Of 420 records, 396 women had a valid Hb (85, 21.5 percent, below 11.0 g/dL) and 410 a valid mid-upper arm circumference (111, 27.1 percent, at risk of CED). Hb and MUAC were excluded from the feature sets, and imputation, feature selection, tuning and thresholds were fitted inside nested repeated cross-validation (5 x 5 outer, 3-fold inner). XGBoost was evaluated against pre-specified baselines and compared with four other boosting algorithms (GBM, LightGBM, CatBoost, AdaBoost) under an identical protocol. For CED, XGBoost reached an AUC-ROC of 0.773 (0.719 to 0.823) but did not exceed Logistic Regression (difference -0.021 (-0.049 to 0.007), 97.5% CI). Hb could not be estimated better than the mean (XGBoost MAE 0.998 (0.929 to 1.071) g/dL; the R² point estimate was below 0 for every model), so anemia screening from predicted Hb did not reach its feasibility criteria. The five boosting algorithms did not differ meaningfully on either target. All four pre-specified hypotheses were not supported. SHAP rankings agreed closely across algorithms, with pre-pregnancy weight ranked first for both targets. A Streamlit prototype presents the CED estimate as the main result and the Hb estimate as indicative only.

## 1. Methods

### 1.1 Data and participants

Raw records: 420. Exact duplicate records removed: 1. Records without any usable target removed: 1. Hb recorded as 0 was treated as not measured (16 women, 15 of whom reported never having had a blood test). Hb above 20 g/dL was removed from the Hb analysis (7). Invalid MUAC values: 9. Eligible records: 396 for the Hb model and 410 for the CED model (source: reports/tables/a01).

| Outcome | Eligible | Cases | Percent | Detail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Anemia (Hb < 11.0 g/dL) | 396 | 85 | 21.5 | mild 57, moderate 28, severe 0 |
| CED risk (MUAC < 23.5 cm) | 410 | 111 | 27.1 | recorded MUAC of 23 cm or less |

### 1.2 Features

Eleven questionnaire candidates: Age (years), Number of children, Children under 5, Pre-pregnancy weight (kg), Height (cm), ANC visits, HFIAS score (0-27), Education, Monthly income, Egg consumption, Food taboo. The HFIAS score is the sum of the nine HFIAS items. In every training split, mutual information and random forest importance (300 trees) ranks were averaged; Pre-pregnancy weight (kg), ANC visits, HFIAS score (0-27) were always kept and the best remaining features completed a set of 7. Imputation (median for numeric, mode for ordinal and binary) was fitted inside each training split. Hb, MUAC, their labels and identifiers are refused by a guard at fit and at prediction time.

### 1.3 Models

Main model: XGBoost (regressor for Hb, classifier for CED). Pre-specified baselines: mean-only and Ridge (Hb), class proportion and Logistic Regression (CED). Exploratory comparators: Decision Tree and Random Forest. Boosting comparators (supervisor revision): Gradient Boosting Machine (scikit-learn), LightGBM, CatBoost and AdaBoost (SAMME for classification, AdaBoost.R2 for regression, shallow decision trees as base learners). All models received the same integer-coded matrix; CatBoost's native categorical handling was not used. No resampling was used in the main models. Search spaces are listed in Appendix A.

### 1.4 Validation and tuning

Repeated stratified 5-fold cross-validation with 5 repetitions on all eligible records, stratified on anemia class x CED status. Inside each outer training set an inner 3-fold cross-validation was used for Optuna tuning (30 TPE trials with a fixed seed for every tuned model; objective MAE for Hb and AUC-ROC for CED) and to produce the predictions that set the decision threshold: the cut-off on predicted Hb that flags 70% of true anemia cases, and Youden's index for CED. Thresholds never used the outer test fold or predictions of a model on its own training rows. Every model used identical outer folds, inner folds, preprocessing and per-fold feature sets.

### 1.5 Statistical analysis

For each repetition the five outer test folds were pooled, so each woman has one out-of-fold prediction per repetition. Metrics were computed on the pooled predictions with percentile bootstrap intervals over women (2000 resamples per repetition); point estimates and CI bounds were averaged over the five repetitions. Comparisons resampled the same women for both models (paired bootstrap). The corrected resampled t-test (Nadeau and Bengio) is reported as an approximate check only. Holm's procedure was applied across the two primary hypotheses (first judged at a 97.5 percent CI) and, for reporting only, across the four XGBoost-versus-comparator differences per target on MAE (Hb) or AUC-ROC (CED).

### 1.6 Pre-specified hypotheses

| Hypothesis | Criterion |
|---|---|
| P1_anemia_screening | Sensitivity of at least 0.70 and specificity of at least 0.40 on out-of-fold predictions, with the lower bound of the AUC confidence interval above 0.50. |
| P2_ced_classification | AUC of at least 0.70 with a confidence interval lower bound of at least 0.50, and at least 0.03 AUC above Logistic Regression. |
| S1_hb_vs_mean | MAE lower by at least 0.10 g/dL. |
| S2_hb_vs_ridge | MAE lower by at least 0.05 g/dL. |

### 1.7 Explanations

SHAP values were computed with shap.TreeExplainer only (no KernelExplainer fallback). For every boosting model, the 25 outer-fold models were refitted from their stored hyperparameters, had to reproduce the stored out-of-fold predictions, and were explained on their outer test folds. Additivity was checked against a tolerance of 0.0001 in raw output units (g/dL, log-odds). Stability is the mean pairwise Spearman correlation of mean |SHAP| across fold models; agreement between algorithms is the Spearman correlation of their rankings.

### 1.8 Selection of the dashboard model

Candidates: XGBoost, GBM, LightGBM, CatBoost, AdaBoost; baselines, Decision Tree and Random Forest are never selected. A candidate is eligible only with a valid TreeExplainer and additivity passed on all 25 fold models. Version 1 of the rule (locked 2026-10-27, before the four comparators were run) preferred XGBoost whenever its paired 95 percent CI against the best eligible model contained 0. **Version 2 (2026-10-28, a deviation decided after all results were known)** selects the eligible model with the best point estimate (MAE for Hb, AUC-ROC for CED) with no preferred model. The selection is therefore post hoc and its performance optimistic. The Hb explanation is shown only if the selected Hb model reduces MAE versus mean-only by at least 0.10 g/dL (same rule as S1).

### 1.9 Safeguards and reproducibility

Canaries before any headline result: label permutation (AUC must stay at or below 0.60, Hb R² at or below 0.05) and a fit spy recording the rows seen by every fit; results that look too good (CED AUC above 0.90, Hb R² above 0.50) stop the analysis. Each outer fold is checkpointed under a hash of the configuration, hypotheses, raw data and source code. A refactor of the engine was rerun and every output compared cell for cell with the earlier results (identical). The automated test suite covers leakage, identical folds across models, two-run reproducibility, the selection rule and the dashboard.

### 2.9 Training and inference cost

Difference = variant minus comparator; reduction = comparator minus variant (a negative MAE reduction means the variant had the larger error). A positive Brier difference means the variant was worse calibrated.

Calibration of the selected CED model (XGBoost): Brier uncalibrated minus Platt -0.0015 (-0.0036 to 0.0004); the pre-specified rule keeps the uncalibrated probability. Split-conformal 90 percent intervals for Hb (GBM): coverage all 0.90; anemic (Hb < 11) 0.70; not anemic 0.96, which is why the dashboard shows no Hb range (sources: results/exploratory/x13, x14, x16).

## 3. Discussion points (draft, for the author to verify and expand)

- The questionnaire carries a usable signal for CED risk (every model AUC-ROC around 0.77 against 0.50 for the class-proportion model) but practically none for hemoglobin: no algorithm, linear or boosted, improved on predicting the mean.
- Algorithm choice mattered little. The highest CED AUC-ROC point estimate came from Logistic Regression (0.794), and the five boosting algorithms were within about 0.01 of each other with paired CIs that all contained 0. The limit appears to be the information in the features, not the learner.
- The XGBoost-specific hypotheses were not supported. P2 failed only on the margin over Logistic Regression, while its absolute AUC criteria were met.
- SHAP rankings were consistent across algorithms (Spearman 0.93 to 1.00), so the explanation shown in the dashboard does not hinge on the algorithm. Pre-pregnancy weight dominating CED is plausible because it reflects the nutritional status and body mass that MUAC also measures; this is association, not cause.
- The dashboard model was selected after the results were known (version 2 of the rule). The Hb choice of GBM over XGBoost rests on a 0.006 g/dL difference that is not statistically established and does not change what the dashboard can claim about Hb.

## 4. Limitations

- Internal validation on one regional dataset of fewer than 420 women; no external or temporal validation.
- Only 85 anemia cases, so sensitivity estimates have wide intervals.
- Self-reported pre-pregnancy weight and ANC visits; Hb dates differ from interview dates (see the date-gap analyses).
- The dashboard model selection (version 2) was decided after the results were known and is optimistic.
- Sensitivity analyses cover XGBoost and the baselines only, not the four boosting comparators or the selected Hb model.
- AdaBoost could not be explained with TreeExplainer in the installed shap version and was not eligible for the dashboard.
- Equal tuning budgets (30 trials) explore large search spaces (LightGBM, 8 parameters) less thoroughly than small ones.
- No user study with community cadres; dashboard claims are limited to technical correctness.

## 5. Reproducibility

Library versions: python 3.11.6, numpy 1.26.4, pandas 2.2.3, scipy 1.13.1, sklearn 1.5.2, imblearn 0.12.4, xgboost 2.1.3, lightgbm 4.5.0, catboost 1.2.7, shap 0.46.0, smogn 0.1.2, optuna 4.1.0, statsmodels 0.14.4, matplotlib 3.9.2, yaml 6.0.2, joblib 1.4.2, streamlit 1.40.1.
